answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation on work that costs real resources: an agent must lock a copper stake before joining a market, and its earnings flow through a delta that shrinks payouts for brand-new identities while rewarding a long history of verified deliveries. Like a reef, the economy grows by accretion — trust compounds slowly, identity is expensive to fake at scale, and a sybil swarm starves because each fake must pay the same entry cost without ever earning the compounded trust of the real one.
